multiplechoiceresponse.p: An AI-drafted customer email says "we will refund the full amount within 48 hours". You have not confirmed the refund policy. What is the correct action?

choice.div: Remove or correct the commitment before sending; only the policy owner can promise it.
Send it — the customer will be happy.
Add "subject to policy" and send unchanged.

div.p: Commitments are the expensive error in outbound email. The person sending owns the promise, so it must match the policy.

multiplechoiceresponse.p: Which output needs a second reader before it leaves the team?

choice.div: An external proposal containing a price and a delivery date.
An internal note summarizing your own meeting.
A draft agenda for a team stand-up.

div.p: Price and date are commitments with financial consequence. Internal, reversible text can be checked by its author.

multiplechoiceresponse.p: You ask for a spreadsheet formula. What is the minimum check before using it?

choice.div: Run it on a row where you know the answer, including blanks and zeros.
Confirm that it looks complicated enough to be right.
Ask the model whether it is correct.

div.p: A formula is code. Test it against known values and edge cases before it touches real data.

choiceresponse.p: Which are appropriate review gates? Select all that apply.

choice.div: External email with a promise — second reader.
Policy answer — check the policy document itself.
Meeting summary — the meeting owner confirms decisions and dates.
Financial formula — peer review before use.
Any AI output — no review needed if the model is new.

div.p: Each gate matches the consequence of the output. A newer model does not remove the need for review.
